items.title: Concentration's and Wisdom's Marks — Solitude Genuinely Loved, Knowledge Spanning Every Field

items.zh: 能引義利大事務中，尚無深倦，何況小事。如是等類，當知名為菩薩精進波羅蜜多種姓相。云何菩薩靜慮波羅蜜多種姓相？謂諸菩薩，性於法義能審思惟，無多散亂。若見若聞阿練若處、山巖、林藪、邊際臥具人不狎習離惡眾生，隨順宴默。便生是念：是處安樂，出離、遠離。常於出離及遠離所深生愛慕。性薄煩惱，諸蓋輕微，麁重羸弱。至遠離處，思量自義，心不極為諸惡尋思之所纏擾。於其怨品，尚能速疾安住慈心，況於親品及中庸品。
items.en: Amid great undertakings that bring genuine benefit to beings, one feels no deep weariness whatsoever — how much less over small matters … bodhisattvas, by nature, are able to reflect carefully on the meaning of the teaching, with little scattered distraction … one gives rise to the thought: this place is peaceful, a place of renunciation and seclusion — and comes to deeply cherish renunciation and seclusion always … towards even an enemy, one is quickly able to abide in a mind of loving-kindness — how much more so towards a friend, or someone neutral.

items.zh: 若見若聞有苦眾生，為種種苦之所逼惱，起大悲心，於彼眾生隨能隨力方便拔濟，令離眾苦。於諸眾生，性自樂施利益安樂。親屬衰亡、喪失財寶、殺縛禁閉及驅擯等諸苦難中，悉能安忍。其性聰敏，於法能受、能持、能思；成就念力，於久所作、所說事中，能自記憶，亦令他憶。如是等類，當知名為菩薩靜慮波羅蜜多種姓相。云何菩薩慧波羅蜜多種姓相？
謂諸菩薩成俱生慧，能入一切明處境界。性不頑鈍、性不微昧、性不愚癡。遍於彼彼離放逸處有力思擇。
items.en: Bodhisattvas possess an innate wisdom, able to enter every field of knowledge. By nature neither dull, nor obscured, nor deluded, they are everywhere able, with real strength, to discern and step away from occasions of heedlessness.

items.zh: 如是等類，當知名為菩薩慧波羅蜜多種姓相。應知是名能比菩薩種姓麁相。決定實義，唯佛世尊究竟現見。由諸菩薩所有種姓性，與如是功德相應，成就賢善諸白淨法。

items.title: Section: Why Buddhahood Itself Is Genuinely Inconceivable — Five Aspects, Two Reasons

items.zh: 是故能與難得最勝不可思議無動無上如來果位為證得因，應正道理，餘不應理。
items.en: For this reason, this lineage alone is able to serve as the cause for attaining the Tathāgata's fruit — a fruit hard to attain, most excellent, inconceivable, unmoving, and unsurpassed. This accords with correct principle; any other claim does not.

items.zh: 種姓菩薩，乃至未為白法相違四隨煩惱若具不具之所染污，性與如是白法相應。

items.title: Even a Fallen Bodhisattva Differs — Brief Suffering, Swift Return, Compassion Kindled Rather Than Crushed

items.zh: 若被染污，如是白法皆不顯現，或於一時生諸惡趣。菩薩雖生諸惡趣中，由種姓力，應知與餘生惡趣者有大差別。
items.en: If corrupted by affliction, none of these wholesome qualities appear, and one may, at some point, be reborn into a lower destiny. Yet even reborn there, by the sheer force of that lineage, one should know a bodhisattva differs greatly from any other being reborn in such a place.

items.zh: 謂彼菩薩久處生死，或時時間生諸惡趣，雖暫生彼，速能解脫；雖在惡趣，而不受於猛利苦受，如餘有情生惡趣者；雖觸微苦，而能發生增上厭離，於生惡趣受苦有情，深起悲心。
items.en: Such a bodhisattva, long abiding in the cycle of birth and death, may from time to time be reborn into a lower destiny — but even reborn there only briefly, is swiftly able to gain release; and though present there, does not undergo the fierce, sharp suffering that other beings reborn there endure; and though touched by some slight suffering, is thereby moved to heightened revulsion, and gives rise to deep compassion for the suffering beings reborn there.

items.zh: 如是等事，皆由種姓。佛大悲因之所熏發，是故當知，種姓菩薩雖生惡趣，然與其餘生惡趣者有大差別。何等名為種姓菩薩白法相違四隨煩惱？

items.title: Four Afflictions That Corrupt Lineage, and Four Conditions That Slow Its Fruit

items.zh: 謂放逸者，由先串習諸煩惱故，性成猛利、長時煩惱，是名第一隨煩惱姓。又愚癡者、不善巧者，依附惡友，是名第二隨煩惱性。又為尊長、夫主、王賊及怨敵等所拘逼者，不得自在，其心迷亂，是名第三隨煩惱性。又資生具有匱乏者，顧戀身命，是名第四隨煩惱性。
items.en: Heedlessness: through previously habituated afflictions, one's afflictions become fierce and long-lasting … delusion and lack of skill: relying on bad companions … being restrained or coerced by superiors, a spouse, a ruler, bandits, or enemies, one loses freedom and the mind becomes confused … and being deprived of life's basic necessities, one clings anxiously to body and life — this is the fourth kind of derivative affliction.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩雖具種姓，由四因緣，不能速證阿耨多羅三藐三菩提。何等為四？謂諸菩薩，先未值遇諸佛菩薩真善知識，為說菩提無顛倒道。如是名為第一因緣。又諸菩薩，雖遇善友為說正道，而顛倒執，於諸菩薩正所學中顛倒修學。如是名為第二因緣。又諸菩薩，雖遇善友為說正道，於諸菩薩正所學中無倒修學，而於加行方便慢緩、懈怠嬾惰，不成勇猛、熾然精進。如是名為第三因緣。又諸菩薩，雖遇善友為說正道，於諸菩薩正所學中無倒修學，亦於加行勇猛精進，然諸善根猶未成熟，菩提資糧未得圓滿，未於長時積習所有菩提分法。如是名為第四因緣。如是菩薩雖有種姓，因緣闕故，不能速證無上菩提。若具因緣，便能速證。若無種姓補特伽羅，雖有一切，一切一切種，當知決定不證菩提。復次，
items.en: Bodhisattvas, though possessing the lineage, may fail to swiftly attain unsurpassed, perfect awakening for four reasons: not yet having encountered a genuine spiritual friend among the buddhas and bodhisattvas … having encountered one, yet clinging to a distorted understanding of what is taught … having encountered one and understood correctly, yet remaining slack, lazy, and indolent in actual practice … or having understood correctly and practised diligently, yet with wholesome roots still unripe and the provisions for awakening not yet complete. But a person without the lineage, even with every one of these conditions present — all such beings, of every kind across the realms and destinies — should be understood as certain never to attain awakening at all.

blocks.text: The remaining marks, then why even a fallen bodhisattva differs from others. A short passage (0479c27) is untranslated.

"Amid great undertakings for beings' benefit, one feels no deep weariness, how much less over small matters." "By nature able to reflect carefully on the meaning of the teaching, with little scattering." "Towards even an enemy, one quickly abides in loving-kindness."
"An innate wisdom, able to enter every field of knowledge; by nature neither dull nor deluded."
"This lineage alone is the cause for attaining the Tathāgata's fruit: hard to attain, most excellent, inconceivable, unmoving, unsurpassed."

"If corrupted by affliction, none of these qualities appear, and one may be reborn in a lower destiny. Yet even there, by the force of the lineage", one differs from others: one is released quickly (Master Cháng Bǎi: "like a ball, it bounces back"); does not suffer as fiercely; feels revulsion; and is moved to compassion for others there.

Heedlessness (fierce afflictions from habit); delusion (relying on bad companions; Venerable Miào Jìng: "near vermilion one turns red"); being coerced by superiors, a spouse, a ruler, bandits, enemies; and destitution, clinging anxiously to life.

Not yet meeting a true spiritual friend; meeting one but "clinging to a distorted understanding of what is taught"; understanding correctly, but "slack and lazy in practice"; or practising diligently, "yet with wholesome roots unripe and the provisions not complete". One without the lineage, even with all these conditions, never attains awakening.

quiz.q: "Reflecting carefully on the teaching, with little distraction." How does Venerable Miào Jìng map calm and insight?
options: careful reflection is insight; little distraction is calm
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas, by nature, are able to reflect carefully on the meaning of the teaching, with little scattered distraction." Venerable Miào Jìng: "able to reflect carefully" is insight; "little distraction" is calm.

quiz.q: "Towards even an enemy, quickly abiding in loving-kindness." Why is this possible, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the seed of compassion is strong — towards foe, friend, and neutral alike
quiz.why: "Towards even an enemy, one is quickly able to abide in a mind of loving-kindness — how much more so towards a friend, or someone neutral." Master Cháng Bǎi: because the seed of compassion is strong, one can extend kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity to all three — foe, friend, neutral.

quiz.q: "Innate wisdom, able to enter every field of knowledge." How does Venerable Miào Jìng divide this?
options: innate wisdom is inborn; entering every field is cultivated wisdom
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas possess an innate wisdom, able to enter every field of knowledge." Venerable Miào Jìng: innate wisdom is wisdom gained at birth; "able to enter every field of knowledge" is wisdom gained through cultivation.

quiz.q: The Tathāgata's fruit is "hard to attain." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain?
options: it takes three incalculable eons of accumulating merit and wisdom
quiz.why: "This lineage alone is able to serve as the cause for attaining the Tathāgata's fruit — a fruit hard to attain, most excellent, inconceivable, unmoving, and unsurpassed." Master Cháng Bǎi: it takes three incalculable eons of long accumulating merit and wisdom to achieve — hence "hard to attain."

quiz.q: A bodhisattva in a lower destiny "is swiftly able to gain release." What image does Master Cháng Bǎi use?
options: like a ball, quickly bouncing back up
quiz.why: "Even reborn there only briefly, is swiftly able to gain release." Master Cháng Bǎi: like a ball, it bounces right back up.

quiz.q: "Through previously habituated afflictions, they become fierce and long-lasting." How does Venerable Miào Jìng illustrate habituation?
quiz.why: "Heedlessness: through previously habituated afflictions, one's afflictions become fierce and long-lasting." Venerable Miào Jìng: you lost your temper yesterday, and today you lose it again.

quiz.q: "The deluded and unskilled rely on bad companions." What saying does Venerable Miào Jìng cite?
options: near vermilion turns red, near ink turns black
quiz.why: "Delusion and lack of skill: relying on bad companions." Venerable Miào Jìng: near vermilion one turns red; near ink one turns black.
